title: Absence Is a Type
goal: No null in Rust. A value that might be missing is an Option.

sections.text: Rust has no null. When a value might be absent, the function returns `Option<T>`: either `Some(value)` or `None`. The possibility of absence is written in the type, so the compiler forces every caller to handle it. Forgetting the empty case becomes a compile error instead of a runtime crash.

sections.caption: The signature tells the caller the truth.

sections.text: The escape hatch `.unwrap()` takes the value out of a `Some` and panics on a `None`. It turns a possible absence into a certain crash. Sometimes that is acceptable in a test or a prototype. In API code, prefer to keep the `Option` and let the caller decide.

You rarely need to open an `Option` by hand. Combinators work inside it: `.map()` transforms the value if there is one and passes `None` through. `.and_then()` chains a second operation that can itself fail. `.unwrap_or(default)` ends a chain with a fallback. The puzzles in this deck train you to stay inside the `Option` until the last step.

explanation: Option<T> makes absence part of the type. Prefer combinators like map and unwrap_or over unwrap.
